dossier.public_summary: The 13.5-day dip averages about 420 ppm and looks flat-bottomed, but its depth jumps from near-zero to over 1,600 ppm from sector to sector and from one transit to the next, with two transits over 2,300 ppm dominating the signal. That strong inconsistency, plus a marginal odd-even difference and a marginal secondary, is not expected for a planet on the target star and points to the few strong events and systematics creating a spurious period.

reasons.why: Depth varies well beyond calibration scatter and detector systematics, including within the same SPOC source, indicating the ‘average’ 418.1 ppm dip is not steady like a planet on the target star.
reasons.value: verdict: changes_within_a_source, p_constant_all: 1.1879369107464585e-28, SPOC 2-min p_constant: 2.5223144096257244e-21, TESS-SPOC p_constant: 3.5187928639349026e-09

reasons.why: The signal is dominated by a few much deeper outliers; many transits are flat/negative and depths are wildly inconsistent, so a few bad events create the 17.9 SNR period rather than a consistent planetary transit.
reasons.value: 23 transits, p_consistent: 1.0474604489501634e-74, share_of_top_3: 0.852, mean depth 420 ppm with single transits 2387 ppm at epoch -53 (sigma 11.4) and 2343 ppm at epoch 69 (sigma 10.5)

reasons.why: Sector-to-sector depths scatter over ~0 to ~1646 ppm with depth_change_pct 360.2 and chi2 160.2 dof 11, impossible for an on-target planet to show that much variation; consistent with spots/systematics or a blended EB sampled differently by apertures.

Marginal odd/even offset (~2 sigma brighter odds) and marginal secondary at phase 0.666 near peak brightening ambiguity hint at binary-like modulation, supporting the variability interpretation over a flat-bottomed planet (shape v_sigma -2.408, fit b 0.9665, ratio 0.8189 otherwise look planet-like).
reasons.value: odd_even diff_sigma 2.95 depth_odd_ppm 520 depth_even_ppm 312.3 depth_ratio 1.7, secondary snr 4.499 depth_ppm 94.67 at phase 0.666, best_brightening_snr 4.801

reasons.why: A faint neighbour could still be diluted, and the inconclusive centroid plus huge depth scatter gives no positive evidence the dip is on-target; with the scatter, a blended EB that appears shallow in some sectors and deep in others is more plausible than a planet, even though there is no star within 1 pixel that plausibly causes the average 418 ppm dip without deep eclipse.
